short_description: Even if the system is usable without docs, help should be easy to find, task-focused, and concise.

positive.definition: Help center is searchable and surfaces relevant articles
positive.evidence_required: name the surface and the search affordance

positive.definition: Tooltips, inline hints, or guided tours appear at the point of need
positive.evidence_required: name the surface and the help element

positive.definition: Help articles are organized around user tasks rather than system features
positive.evidence_required: name the article and the task it addresses

positive.definition: Help content is concise and scannable (bullets, headings, code snippets)
positive.evidence_required: name the article and the structure

positive.definition: Help link is reachable from anywhere via persistent control (help icon, ? in command palette)

negative.definition: No help, docs, or tooltips exist where users would clearly need them
negative.evidence_required: name the surface and the missing help

negative.definition: Help is reachable only through deep navigation or external link
Help is organized by feature surfaces rather than by user task
Help articles are dense walls of text with no structure

critical_negative.definition: Surface that frequently blocks users (auth, payment, error) has no help, no FAQ, no support contact
